items.title: Melaka BN told not to underestimate rivals in state election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Melaka Barisan Nasional candidates and election machinery have been reminded not to become complacent or underestimate their opponents in the upcoming state election on Nov 14. "Never become complacent. Earlier, Rauf launched the Kota Melaka parliamentary-level BN election machinery for the 16th Melaka election and joined a motorcycle convoy of more than 100 riders to the launch site at Taman Bukit Punggur, Telok Mas.

items.title: Police bust online gaming scam syndicate operating from abandoned hotel
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: Police have dismantled an online gaming scam syndicate masterminded by Bangladeshi citizens operating out of an abandoned hotel in Taman Lagenda Indah here. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the syndicate is believed to have operated since June, using a dedicated website and WhatsApp to communicate with clients, also believed to be Bangladeshi nationals. Hanyan said the four detained Bangladeshi men each earned about RM2,700 per month.

items.title: PKR takes aim at ‘Big Brother’ Umno as MCA walkout exposes deeper BN rifts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The move by MCA to walk out of an event to unveil Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates for the 16th Melaka state election Saturday night has raised questions regarding the sincerity of its coalition partner, Umno, in their political cooperation. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said this situation also casts doubt on the foundation of BN’s political alliances with other parties, questioning whether they are built on principles and trust, or merely on political interests and power. “If MCA, a long-standing BN component party, feels disrespected, what does this mean for other parties that have entered into cooperation with BN?

items.title: Police advise public to avoid Bagan Lalang beach over crocodile sighting
items.summary: Sepang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report yesterday afternoon of an animal believed to be a crocodile spotted near a beach resort. "For the safety of residents and tourists, police advise the public to refrain from activities along Bagan Lalang beach in Sungai Pelek," he said in a statement today. Norhizam said police will collaborate with relevant agencies to monitor the situation and take appropriate measures to ensure public safety.

items.title: Perikatan confirms using own logo for Melaka election as tensions with Bersatu mount
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will initiate disciplinary proceedings against Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) over actions deemed contrary to the coalition’s interests. He said the article empowered the PN Supreme Council to take disciplinary action against any member party, individual member, affiliated party or associate member found to have acted against the coalition’s interests. “The PN Supreme Council has the authority to take disciplinary action against any member party, individual member, affiliated party, or associate member by issuing a warning, suspending, or expelling the party or member concerned if they engage in conduct contrary to PN’s interests.

items.title: After TuJu flop, Lim Guan Eng wants open tender for Malaysian-made Waze rival
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — DAP chairman and Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today called for an open tender to develop a new local navigation application as an alternative to Waze, saying the government should replace what he described as the failed TuJu app. In a statement, Lim said TuJu had become a “national embarrassment” and questioned why Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB), the company behind the application, was awarded the project without an open tender. “TuJu has failed miserably and Malaysians are asking why Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB), the private company behind the TuJu navigation app, was given the approval without an open tender,” he said.

items.title: PH banks on track record in three states to win Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is banking on its experience governing Selangor, Penang and Negri Sembilan as it seeks to win over voters in the Nov 14 Melaka election. Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin said PH had experience managing the administrations in the three states and hoped Melaka voters would give the coalition the same opportunity. He said PH believed its governing experience could serve as a foundation for leading Melaka.

items.title: Penang landslide strikes BMW and Honda City near Leisure Bay Condominium in Tanjung Tokong
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 26 — Two cars were badly damaged after being buried in a landslide near 33 Leisure Bay Condominium, Jalan Tanjung Tokong, Tanjung Bungah here yesterday. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations and Firefighting Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 6.50 pm before a team from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 7 pm. “Rescue and monitoring operations are still underway, involving six personnel, including a supervisor and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), with assistance from the police at the scene,” he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: Lula defies odds to win fourth term as Brazil president
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil's leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who trounced him in the first round. With Lula's victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries – such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru – all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump. After a campaign marred by scandal and mud-slinging, Sunday's vote plunged into chaos after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extending voting by two hours, at the request of Lula who said buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting.

items.title: Sarawak election countdown begins with assembly dissolution today, EC meeting next
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 26 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly was officially dissolved today, paving the way for the 13th Sarawak State Election. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution on Friday (Oct 23) after receiving the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar. GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples’ Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.

items.title: Storms wreak havoc across Europe, disrupting power, flights and phones
items.summary: LONDON: Storms battered northern Europe Sunday, killing a man, cutting power to more than 150,000 homes and disrupting travel and phone networks. Trees and power cables brought down by the storm blocked roads and rail lines across Scotland and northern England. The powerful winds also battered northern France across the Channel as Europe battled its first big autumn storms of the year.

items.title: Sarawak assembly dissolved, paving way for state election
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak assembly was officially dissolved today, paving the way for the 13th state election. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution on Friday after receiving the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar. GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.

items.title: 2,670 displaced in Israel's Hebron operation: Palestinian Authority
items.summary: RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Authority said Sunday that nearly 2,700 people had been displaced by an Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron launched after two soldiers were killed in an attack nearby. Following Friday's attack, Israeli forces entered the Hebron neighbourhood of Ein Deir Baha, where the assailants lived, and ordered residents to pack up and leave after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged a major operation in the occupied territory. "More than 2,670 Palestinians have been forcibly displaced from their homes in Hebron by Israeli occupation forces, the majority of them women, children, and elderly people, according to data from Hebron Municipality," the Palestinian prime minister's office said on X.

items.title: Haze eases, most areas record good, moderate air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions across the country continued to improve, with most areas recording good or moderate Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7am today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 29 areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak recorded good API readings, while 32 recorded moderate levels. However, seven areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy air quality, with the Serian district police headquarters monitoring station registering the highest API reading at 173.

items.title: Ringgit higher against US dollar in early trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit was slightly higher against the US dollar in early trade on Monday amid cautious sentiment ahead of the US Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Oct 27-28. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) was seen rising 0.2 per cent while the US Treasury yields were also higher. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Student housing shortage, Syariah Court delays among Dewan Rakyat focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Strategies to strengthen downstream commodity industries, the shortage of accommodation at public university colleges and delays in Syariah Court proceedings are among the issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on Parliament's official website, Datuk Shamshulkahar Mohd Deli (BN-Jempol) will ask the plantation and commodities minister about strategies to strengthen downstream commodity industries. Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail (PH-Bandar Tun Razak) will ask the higher education minister about ongoing efforts to address the shortage of accommodation at public university residential colleges, particularly for students from the B40 income group.

items.title: [UPDATED] Oil slips from near six-months highs despite supply concerns
items.summary: US crude futures were down US$1.60, or 1.55 per cent, at US$101.67 per barrel by 0018 GMT. Brent crude futures were down US$1.56 or 1.34 per cent at US$115.16. Prices had settled nearly US$3 higher on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns.

items.title: Two men held over nearly 20,000 sticks of smuggled cigarettes seized in Tanah Merah
items.summary: TANAH MERAH: Two men, including a Pakistani, were arrested after nearly 20,000 sticks of smuggled cigarettes were seized in two separate raids yesterday. Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the first raid was conducted at a house in Kampung Bukit Nangka, Gual Ipoh, at 4pm. Radzi said the second raid was conducted at a shop-house in Kampung Paralla Dua at 5pm.

items.title: Trump says Canada tariff deal coming 'soon' at Michigan border rally
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump at a Sunday political rally predicted a trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics. At an event in Port Huron, Michigan, to boost Republican candidates ahead of the Nov 3 midterms, Trump and other speakers reiterated his oft-expressed position that higher tariffs on Canadian goods are needed because Canada "has been ripping off" the US in trade. "I had to do it," Trump told the Michigan crowd.

items.title: US helped Gulf nations ship 1.5 billion barrels through Hormuz
items.summary: RIYADH: US Central Command on Sunday said it helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via the Strait of Hormuz since summer, bypassing an Iranian blockade. "U.S. forces reach the milestone of assisting Gulf partners in exporting more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer," CENTCOM said in a statement posted on X. "Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people," said CENTCOM chief admiral Brad Cooper, who was visiting US troops in Hormuz.

items.title: Malaysia makes progress in graft fight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has completed 41 of the 60 sub-strategies under the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (NACS) 2024-2028, marking progress in efforts to strengthen governance and combat corruption. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) National Governance Planning Division Senior Director Datuk Idris Zaharudin said the achievement reflected the government's efforts to translate policy commitments into concrete action across ministries and agencies. Launched in May 2024 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, NACS provides a comprehensive framework to strengthen governance, integrity and accountability through legislative reforms, institutional improvement, the integration of anti-corruption education into school and university curricula, and stronger private sector accountability through corporate integrity programmes.

items.title: Malaysia's 'green' test: Billions pledged, too few bankable
items.summary: Delays, infrastructure bottlenecks and financing constraints risk slowing the energy transition. However, only around US$315 billion is on a credible path to deployment, Shahril said. Bain's 2026 report on Southeast Asia's green economy found that 50 to 60 per cent of renewable energy projects in Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia were cancelled between 2021 and 2025, Shahril said.

items.title: Vista sees stronger private aviation demand in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vista's flight traffic in Malaysia rose 18 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, higher than the 14 per cent growth recorded across Asia Pacific. Vista chief business officer Youssef Mouallem said the growth is supported by industrial activity in Malaysia and demand from business travellers seeking greater flexibility and shorter travel time. Mouallem said private aviation demand in Malaysia is growing faster than the wider Asia Pacific market and he expects the trend to continue in the second half of the year.

items.title: Share upside as plantation stocks draw attention on earnings, dividends
items.summary: SD Guthrie follows with a target price of RM7.81, representing a 36.5 per cent upside from RM5.72 (Oct 20), while Genting Plantations has a target price of RM6.84, implying a 34.1 per cent gain from RM5.10 (Oct 20), the firm said in a recent note. It said Sarawak Plantation offers a potential upside of 27.9 per cent, with a target price of RM5.59 against its price of RM4.37 (Oct 20). Sarawak Plantation follows at 6.9 per cent, while Genting Plantations offers 5.8 per cent.

items.title: Zelenskyy: US-Ukraine-Russia meeting to take place in November
items.summary: KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday said that a trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow would take place in November aiming to restart stalled peace talks. All this can therefore be discussed in November," Zelenskyy said in an interview with Ukrainian television. On Friday Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that a trilateral meeting was planned to take place in the United Arab Emirates in November.

items.title: Malaysia's missing economic map
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia measures what its states produce. Malaysia already publishes national input-output accounts and has valuable regional research. States Apart, Factories Together Penang and Kedah are separate jurisdictions but increasingly connected production locations.

items.title: Building costs soar, but Mah Sing limits increase to 10pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rising building material prices are putting pressure on property developers to protect profit margins without pricing homebuyers out of the market, as industry players grapple with reported increases of 20 per cent to 30 per cent in selected construction inputs. However, the impact on overall project costs varies depending on the materials used, their contribution to total construction expenses and developers' ability to negotiate competitive procurement terms, according to Mah Sing Group Bhd founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum. Leong said the group's overall construction costs had increased by an estimated 5.0 per cent to 10 per cent, significantly below the reported price hikes for certain building materials.

items.title: 'Marine has to win': Le Pen supporters fear France is in decline
items.summary: ORLÉANS, France: Wrapped in the French tricolour, Loic Le Tourneau was among thousands of supporters who flocked on Sunday to see far-right leader Marine Le Pen officially launch her presidential campaign. Le Tourneau, who travelled nearly an hour to attend the rally, said he was increasingly worried about insecurity in France – even though he said he had not experienced it firsthand in the countryside where he lives. Polls show Le Pen – who has already made three unsuccessful presidential bids – is the frontrunner in the race to succeed centrist President Emmanuel Macron in next year's election.

items.title: Eisenkot takes aim at Netanyahu as Israel heads to polls
items.summary: TEL AVIV: Israeli election contender Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday vowed to unite the country as he held his final major rally before the vote, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sought to tar his main rival as soft on Iran. Polls had showed Netanyahu and Eisenkot running neck and neck before a ban on new polling took effect in the three days before Tuesday's vote. Speaking to an audience of hundreds on Sunday, Eisenkot pledged to heal divisions inside Israeli society after Netanyahu's divisive tenure, and voiced "a commitment to security and the economy."

items.title: Your aircon isn’t cleaning your air, and bowls of water won’t either: What haze does indoors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Keeping windows and doors shut during haze can help limit polluted air entering homes, but it may not be enough to protect occupants from fine particles that seep indoors, two indoor air quality specialists said. Syida Nasri, Airscan’s head of indoor air quality and a Department of Occupational Safety and Health-accredited indoor air quality assessor, said fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less (PM2.5) could enter homes through gaps around windows, doors and other openings, even when they were kept closed. “Merely staying indoors isn’t enough to protect against the haze,” she said.

items.title: Skies are clearing, but weeks indoors can mess with your head: Experts say don’t brush off the signs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — With haze conditions continue to affect parts of the country, mental health experts warn that spending prolonged periods indoors can take a toll on mental health and overall wellbeing. He said people may experience behavioural changes when the haze persists for several days or weeks. Less daylight and exercise can disrupt sleep Brian also said reduced physical activity, exposure to natural daylight and social interaction could affect sleep and emotional wellbeing.

items.title: Brazil braces for result of knife-edge election after voting chaos
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil braced Sunday for the results of a nail-biting election pitting leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, after a last-minute order to extend polling by two hours generated chaos and confusion. It is the final electoral battle for Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday and is hoping to pull off a dramatic turnaround after coming in second to the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro in the first round of voting. The counting of votes from Brazil's electronic machines restarted after a last-minute order from the Supreme Court to extend voting.

items.title: 38,000 women to benefit from mammogram screening subsidies
items.summary: THE National Population and Family Development Board has allocated RM9 million for mammogram screening subsidies, which will benefit 38,000 women. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was part of the government's efforts to encourage more women to undergo early breast cancer screening. Nancy encouraged women to register early to secure screening slots at the available facilities.

items.title: Serbia's student movement ousts longtime leader in parliament poll
items.summary: BELGRADE: Serbia's student-led movement declared victory in parliamentary elections Sunday ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist party. The victory in the snap vote comes after nearly two years of anti-government protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at Novi Sad railway station that killed 16 people. "Preliminary results show that students are convincingly leading in almost all polling stations," Radomir Saicic, a candidate for the Students' List, said in a speech at the movement's election HQ.

items.title: Netanyahu warns Iran may try to disrupt election, says 'don't test us'
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Iran and its allies might try to disrupt Tuesday's Israeli elections, warning the Islamic republic against any hostile acts. The remarks came as Israel's Channel 12 reported, citing unnamed sources, that there had been a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied. "We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections," Netanyahu said in a video released by his office on Sunday.

items.title: Form Six allowance to be paid over 3 semesters
items.summary: FORM Six students will receive a living allowance of RM2,500 starting next year, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. Fadhlina said the initiative reflected the government's commitment to supporting Form Six students and improving the quality of Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia. The amount is equivalent to the allowance received by matriculation students and is expected to benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.

items.title: Trump: Audi to invest US$4.2b in first US plant
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that German automaker Audi planned to invest US$4.2 billion to build its first factory in the US that will produce 200,000 vehicles a year. Audi said the plant would create about 4,500 jobs. Audi, a subsidiary of Volkswagen, said construction was scheduled to begin next year and production in the early 2030s.

items.title: Mislabelled palm oil blends could hurt Malaysia’s reputation abroad, Maritime experts say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Palm oil blended in Malaysia must carry accurate declarations of origin, as any inaccuracy could undermine the integrity and reputation of Malaysian products in international markets, a maritime expert said. Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) Faculty of Maritime Studies senior lecturer Dr Madzli Harun said that while palm oil blending was permitted in the industry, the process did not automatically make the finished product Malaysian in origin. Madzli said blending alone might not satisfy RoO requirements or change a product’s country of origin, and operators must therefore show that the processing carried out meets the relevant criteria before the finished product can be declared Malaysian in origin.

items.title: Sanusi: GE16 will be Pakatan’s last term in Putrajaya and Perikatan’s final term as Opposition
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 25 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has predicted that Pakatan Harapan will lose power in Putrajaya at the 16th general election, according to online reports. He told supporters that PN must use the time left before GE16, expected by December 2027, to strengthen its election machinery. According to Sanusi, a PN government would take a new approach to national development, “developing together with Islam”.

items.title: Zahid, national leaders extend congratulations to Sultan of Selangor on silver jubilee
items.summary: In a Facebook post, Ahmad Zahid prayed that Allah would continue to grant Sultan Sharafuddin good health, well-being and strength to continue providing leadership and protection to the people and state of Selangor. “I pray that Allah SWT will continue to grant Your Royal Highness good health, a blessed life and the strength to continue leading and protecting the state and people of Selangor, with wisdom and compassion for all. “May the state of Selangor remain peaceful, prosperous and blessed under Your Royal Highness’ reign.

items.title: No walk-ins: Finas opens RM15m Creative Content Fund applications online only from Nov 16
items.summary: The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) said applications would be subject to the prevailing Creative Content Fund guidelines and regulations. The six categories include the International Co-Production Fund for Feature Films/Animated Features, First Time Amateur Film Maker (FAME) Fund and Television Programme Co-Production Fund (Supertelefilm). The other categories are the Micro-Drama Co-Production Fund (Broadcasting Stations/OTT Platforms), Veteran Artists Supertelefilm (STAR) Fund and National Public Service Announcement (PSA) Production Fund.

items.title: Dzulkefly: MOH strengthening mental health support nationwide, workplace policy under consultation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is to continue strengthening the support system and access to mental health services nationwide, including through the development of a mental health policy at the workplace, which is currently undergoing an engagement process with stakeholders. MOH is also expanding access to mental health services through 1,116 government health clinics nationwide, in addition to hospitals and community-based services such as Community Mental Health Centres (MENTARI). “This approach also involves over 500 family medicine specialists who provide mental health services at the primary healthcare level,” he said.

items.title: Man found dead outside Cheras food stall; police say no foul play suspected
items.summary: According to The Star , the man was found unconscious at Flat Sri Melaka on Jalan Ikan Emas today, according to Cheras OCPD Asst Comm Mohd Rosdi Daud. An assistant medical officer from Kuala Lumpur Hospital pronounced the man dead at the scene, Mohd Rosdi added. Mohd Rosdi said investigations are ongoing.

items.title: Mardi worker killed by bee swarm while collecting honey at farm in Kemaman
items.summary: Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the incident occurred at 9.50am when the victim, Hafizul Mat, 40, a general worker, was at MARDI’s Kemaman branch at Kilometer 18 of Jalan Ayer Putih with a colleague. Mohd Razi said that while in the tree, the victim shouted at his colleague to run as the bees swarmed him. However, Mohd Razi said the hospital confirmed that the victim died while receiving treatment at 6.42pm.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain in Labuan and six states until 9pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Labuan and six states until 9pm tonight. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the areas affected in Kelantan are Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Pasir Mas and Machang, while in Pahang, they are Jerantut, Kuantan, Maran, Pekan and Lipis. The warning also covers Terengganu, Johor and Sarawak, including Song in Kapit; Kanowit and Sibu in Sibu; Julau and Pakan in Sarikei; Lubok Antu in Sri Aman; Serian; Betong; and Kuching.

items.title: Haze: Eight areas nationwide record unhealthy API as of 6pm, Serian highest at 192
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with Serian IPD in Sarawak recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 192. Unhealthy API readings were also recorded in Terengganu, with Paka registering 156, while Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded 152. Meanwhile, APIMS reported that 50 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 10 areas remained at the good level.

items.title: Police seek dashcam footage, urge witnesses to come forward after crash involving Bernama, NST journalists
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 25 — The police are urging members of the public who witnessed an accident involving a car carrying two journalists and a lorry which occurred this morning on Jalan Ipoh-Lumut, near the Taman Kledang Permai traffic light junction to come forward and assist with the investigation. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those who possess dashcam footage of the incident are also requested to provide the information to the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Ipoh district police headquarters (IPD). He noted that the incident, which took place at approximately 5.45 am., involved a Perodua Bezza carrying the two journalists, who were traveling from the direction of Meru towards Bagan Datuk.

items.title: No piranha found or caught at Klau Dam, but presence not ruled out, says Fisheries Dept
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 25 — No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries Director-General Datuk Adnan Hussain. He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species. “No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program.

items.title: Haze: Johor schools to reopen in phases, starting with exam candidates
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 25 — Schools in Johor will reopen in phases, with the first phase on Monday (tomorrow) and Tuesday limited to students sitting for examinations according to the scheduled timetable. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who places great importance on the safety, health and well-being of the people of Johor. Muhammad Naqib said the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) would coordinate the implementation of health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the wearing of face masks and monitoring of school activities, based on current air pollutant index (API) readings.

items.title: Johor expects 26,000 job opportunities for youth this year, says Onn Hafiz
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 25 — The Johor government expects 26,000 job opportunities to be offered to young people across the state this year, driven by rapid economic growth and the influx of high-value investments. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the projected figure reflected a consistent year-on-year increase, following the success of various strategic initiatives, including the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and large-scale career events such as the Johor Talent Development Council (JTDC) Mega Job Fair. He said the state had continued to record a significant increase in quality job opportunities compared with previous years.

items.title: Four Bangladeshis among six held in Sungai Petani over online gaming scam, syndicate ran from abandoned hotel
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 25 — Police recently arrested six individuals, including four Bangladeshi men, suspected of being involved in an online gaming scam syndicate. Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the syndicate, which operated from an abandoned hotel in Taman Lagenda near here, was believed to have been active since June. “In a raid at 9.30pm on Wednesday (October 21), a team of officers and personnel from the Kuala Muda District Police Headquarters (IPD) Commercial Crime Investigation Division (CCID) arrested four Bangladeshi men aged between 20 and 53.

items.title: Melaka polls: PKR’s seven new faces must earn voters’ trust, says Adam Adli
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 25 — Melaka PKR is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates for next month’s state election, as the party seeks to strengthen support for its reform agenda at the state level. State party acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said PKR needs to work hard to convince voters of the principles and reform agenda it was pursuing at the federal level and ensure they gain acceptance in Melaka. Last night, Prime Minister and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the coalition’s 21 candidates for the state election, comprising nine from PKR, seven from DAP and five from Amanah.

items.title: Haze: 27 schools in Tebedu to close tomorrow, says Sarawak Education Dept
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 25 — Twenty-seven schools in the Tebedu district of Serian will be closed tomorrow due to haze, following continuous monitoring of Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). The Sarawak State Education Department (JPN) said the Oct 26 closure would involve one secondary school and 26 primary schools under its supervision. The Sarawak JPN said that for schools near districts with API readings exceeding 200, headmasters and principals could consider implementing PdPR by taking into account students’ health and safety.

items.title: IGP: Police identify suspects linked to 1.16-tonne ketamine haul found on Malaysian-owned tanker in Indonesian waters
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Police have identified several individuals suspected of being linked to the attempted smuggling of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine found aboard a Malaysian-owned tanker in Indonesian waters recently. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were tracking down the individuals and would strive to make arrests as soon as possible, either today or tomorrow. He said the vessel’s decision to turn back and enter Indonesian waters provided the authorities there with an opportunity to conduct investigations and make arrests.

items.title: Fadhlina orders probe, removes Perak principal from school amid harassment allegations
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has directed the Perak Education Department (JPN) to investigate allegations that a school principal sexually harassed a student. She said the principal has also been temporarily reassigned to the Bagan Datuk District Education Office (PPD) pending the outcome of the investigation, as reported by Harian Metro (HM). The principal has also been placed temporarily at the Bagan Datuk PPD until the investigation is completed,” Fadhlina was quoted as saying.

items.title: FT008 detour near Gua Musang now open to light traffic after sinkhole
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 25 — A temporary detour at FT008 Section 205.556 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road near the Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park here was opened to light vehicles at noon today. The detour, which is part of the Central Spine Road (LTU) Project Packages 3B and 3C, is open only to light vehicles. The FT008 federal road near Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park was closed on Oct 10 following the formation of a sinkhole about eight metres deep.

items.title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu invited to Perikatan talks on RoS case, Melaka polls
items.summary: According to News Straits Times (NST), PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to attend the meeting at PAS headquarters, but whether they would do so was up to them. He said the allocation of the seven seats assigned to PN for the Melaka polls would also be discussed. He said the limited number of seats available meant PN would need to work out a suitable distribution among the parties involved.

items.title: IGP orders immediate CID probe into Noorizwan’s death in custody
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has directed the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to conduct an immediate investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died while in police custody at the Cheras District Police Headquarters (IPD). He said the investigation must be conducted thoroughly following the discovery of several unusual injuries on Noorizwan’s body that warranted further scrutiny. However, police were still awaiting the laboratory report to determine the actual cause of Noorizwan’s death, he added.

items.title: Melaka state polls: PKR’s 30pc women candidates offer voters a more inclusive choice, says Fadhlina
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — PKR’s move to field 30 per cent women candidates in the Melaka state election is part of the party’s strategy to offer voters a more inclusive choice, said Wanita PKR chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said fielding more women candidates could also strengthen women’s representation in state politics. Yesterday, PH chairman and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced 21 candidates to contest in the Melaka state election.

items.title: A split second, a lifetime of loss: Family recalls fatal Paya Terubong landslide
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — A 73-year-old doctor was killed when a landslide struck his family's home in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, trapping him beneath collapsed concrete. The victim, identified as Wong Kar Lin, died when a landslide hit the family’s residence at about 8.36am, trapping him beneath rubble in the kitchen while other family members managed to flee. Poh Lim said only the three of them were at home when the landslide occurred, while the couple’s four children live elsewhere.
